extras.name: Boston
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the harbour and Charles-River shorelines and the parks carry the fit; the 1902 staged sheet is a steep near-vertical view (the grid dense and legible, a printed key of landmarks) spanning the whole city far beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Philadelphia
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Schuylkill and Delaware shorelines and the squares carry the fit; the 1872 staged sheet is the steepest (near-vertical) view staged for the city, drawn from the Schuylkill side with the grid legible to the northern suburbs, spanning well beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Baltimore
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Inner-Harbour and Patapsco shorelines and the parks carry the fit; the 1880 staged sheet is a steep oblique view drawn from the south with the Inner Harbour in the foreground, spanning the whole city beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Pittsburgh
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the river confluence and the bridges carry the fit; the 1902 staged sheet is a steep oblique view drawn from the south with the Allegheny/Monongahela confluence in the foreground and a printed index, spanning the whole city beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent); the name-search trap above applies to this city

extras.name: Cincinnati
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Ohio shoreline and the hillside blocks carry the fit; the 1900 staged sheet is a steep view drawn from the south with the Ohio in the foreground, spanning the whole city and its hillside suburbs beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Louisville
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Ohio and the Kentucky shorelines carry the fit; the 1883 staged sheet is a two-panel composite drawn from the river front (the Kentucky side) - the 1883 International Exposition hall above and the steep near-vertical whole-city view below, the Ohio in the foreground and the grid dense and legible - spanning the whole city beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: St. Louis
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the levee and the Mississippi shoreline carry the fit; the 1858 staged sheet is the steepest (near-vertical) view staged for the city, drawn from the high ground east of the river with the grid legible to the suburbs and the levee and its shipping in the foreground, spanning well beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Chicago
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the lakefront and the river carry the fit; the 1892 staged sheet is a steep near-vertical view drawn from the lake with the grid dense and legible to the horizon, Lake Michigan in the foreground and a printed index, spanning the whole city beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent); the name-search trap above applies to this city

extras.name: Detroit
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Detroit River shoreline and the rail yards carry the fit; the 1889 staged sheet is a steep oblique view drawn from the river covering about three miles square of the central city, the river and its shipping in the foreground, spanning the central city beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)

extras.name: Milwaukee
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the lakefront and the river carry the fit; the 1872 staged sheet is a steep near-vertical view drawn from the lake with the grid dense and legible, Lake Michigan in the lower right and a printed key of landmarks, spanning the whole city beyond the 2000 m town box, so its fit is likely to end a review item (the 236a NY-1811 / DC-ring precedent)
